root_causes: Definitive provider rejection (including game_stop_timeout) and lost RPC shared uncertain outcome. Recovery recognized only child-game-stop IDs, not normal provider-transition IDs; sequence 67 permanently poisoned every later operation.
Bridge's old RLock alone did not serialize effects: stop_game Condition.wait released it while the RPC was still active. A newer binding could enter before the old effect ended.

Child durable-load normalization dropped control_operation. Renew could persist a process token without the matching PID/path/creation time; token presence then suppressed completing the identity tuple. These independently broke restart/expiry cleanup correlation.

Confirmed game stop did not remove the exact old cached running_games entry. A subsequent child start could see session_in_use despite physical idle; an in-flight scan could repopulate obsolete state after a stop.
Retained switching created a new child allowance without reauthorizing the retained control stream's child ID/actor generation. The next provider operation inherited the previous child's identity.
Stream close HTTP 500 or lost reply was not checked against a fresh physical postcondition while holding the same permit.

PowerShell singleton array unwrapping, top-level Force cache reuse and unavailable-source defaults could respectively reject owned idle, serve stale observations or fabricate idle. Inconsistent session telemetry and different running app now also fail closed.

Explicit parent quit/reset relied on profile-matching local retained/resume metadata. When it was absent after a child-to-parent switch or restart, it exited before asking the host for the exact server-owned binding.
